domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Soldered RAM is not an upgrade path
domains.summary: Soldered RAM is not an upgrade path. Many ultrabooks glue LPDDR to the board. Task Manager showing 8 GB does not mean a slot is hiding under a door.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: M.2 slots are not all the same speed
domains.summary: M.2 slots are not all the same speed. An M.2 slot may be SATA, PCIe 3.0×2, or PCIe 4.0×4. The sticker on the drive is not a promise from the board.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Thermal paste is a thin job
domains.summary: Thermal paste is a thin job. Paste fills microscopic gaps between IHS and cooler. A rice-grain or pea in the centre usually spreads under spring pressure.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: A 500 W label is not a 12 V promise
domains.summary: A 500 W label is not a 12 V promise. Modern CPUs and GPUs drink from the 12 V rail. A bargain unit can be 500 W combined and still starve 12 V under a gaming spike.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: RAID is not a backup
domains.summary: RAID is not a backup. RAID 1/5/10 keeps you online after a disk dies. Ransomware, fire, and ‘wrong folder deleted’ laugh at RAID.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: ECC RAM is a different conversation
domains.summary: ECC RAM is a different conversation. ECC catches bit flips. Servers and some workstations want it. Most consumer boards will not even POST with ECC DIMMs.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Clearing CMOS is a blunt instrument
domains.summary: Clearing CMOS is a blunt instrument. A CMOS reset drops custom fan curves, boot order, XMP, and the admin password on many boards — and nothing else.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: USB-C charge is a negotiation
domains.summary: USB-C charge is a negotiation. USB Power Delivery profiles are a handshake. A 100 W brick does not force 100 W into a 45 W laptop, and a charge-only port may refuse video.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: A swollen pack is a safety ticket
domains.summary: A swollen pack is a safety ticket. Li-ion swelling is chemistry failure. It lifts trackpads and cracks glass. Do not puncture, crush, or ‘calibrate it flat’.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: RFC1918 is not ‘the internet’
domains.summary: RFC1918 is not ‘the internet’. 10/8, 172.16/12, and 192.168/16 are private. They are not routable on the public internet without NAT or a tunnel.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: 169.254 means DHCP never answered
domains.summary: 169.254 means DHCP never answered. APIPA is a link-local consolation prize. The host can talk to other APIPA neighbours on the same L2, not to the default gateway.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Ping is not name resolution
domains.summary: Ping is not name resolution. Ping 8.8.8.8 tests a path. Ping office.example tests DNS plus a path. They fail for different reasons.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: An access port is one VLAN, not a vibe
domains.summary: An access port is one VLAN, not a vibe. Access ports untag a single VLAN. Trunks carry many. A phone+PC may want voice VLAN plus data — that is a special case, not ‘set it to.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: A new Wi-Fi generation is not a longer radio
domains.summary: A new Wi-Fi generation is not a longer radio. 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) is about capacity and OFDMA, not magic metres through brick. 5/6 GHz dies on walls faster than 2.4.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Hairpin NAT is a SOHO surprise
domains.summary: Hairpin NAT is a SOHO surprise. Phones on the LAN that try to reach the office by its public name often need NAT loopback. Many cheap routers refuse.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Safe Mode is a diagnostic hat
domains.summary: Safe Mode is a diagnostic hat. Safe Mode loads a minimal set of drivers. If the crash dies in Safe Mode, a third-party driver or autostart is a suspect.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: chmod 777 is not a fix
domains.summary: chmod 777 is not a fix. Linux permissions are owner/group/other with rwx. 777 means everyone can write. That is a welcome mat, not a repair.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: SIP is not a virus scanner
domains.summary: SIP is not a virus scanner. System Integrity Protection stops even root from writing to some system paths. It is a seatbelt, not XProtect’s whole job.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: A corrupted profile is not a dead disk
domains.summary: A corrupted profile is not a dead disk. Windows can boot and still fail one user hive. Other local accounts working is the tell.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Defer is not ‘never’
domains.summary: Defer is not ‘never’. Windows quality vs feature updates, and Intune/WSUS rings, are a schedule. Pausing 35 days is not a security strategy.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Urgency is the payload
domains.summary: Urgency is the payload. Phishing works by compressing time: CEO wants gift cards now. The link is optional; the panic is required.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: MFA prompt spam is an attack
domains.summary: MFA prompt spam is an attack. Fatigue bombing hammers push approvals until a tired human taps Allow. Number matching exists because of this.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Admin every day is a habit, not a need
domains.summary: Admin every day is a habit, not a need. A standard user plus elevation when required beats running as Domain Admin for email.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: A lock screen is a control, not rudeness
domains.summary: A lock screen is a control, not rudeness. Win+L / a short idle policy stops the next person at the hot desk reading payroll.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Delete is not destroy
domains.summary: Delete is not destroy. Recycle Bin and quick format leave recoverables. A drive leaving the building needs a real wipe or physical destroy per policy.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: The queue can be the outage
domains.summary: The queue can be the outage. A stuck job or a dying spooler makes every app look broken. The printer’s ready light is not the whole path.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Dried nozzles are chemistry, not Windows
domains.summary: Dried nozzles are chemistry, not Windows. Infrequent inkjet use clogs. A cleaning cycle wastes ink; a soak is sometimes the honest repair; replacement is sometimes cheaper.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Dot matrix still exists for a reason
domains.summary: Dot matrix still exists for a reason. Impact printers survive multipart carbon forms. Laser will not stamp through three copies.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: ADF and flatbed fail differently
domains.summary: ADF and flatbed fail differently. A double-feed in the ADF is rollers and separation pads. A blotch on every glass scan is the pane, not the driver.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Scope creep is how tickets never close
domains.summary: Scope creep is how tickets never close. ‘While you are here’ is a new ticket. The original symptom still needs a sentence in the close notes.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Prod is not your lab
domains.summary: Prod is not your lab. A firmware flash at 10:00 on a till day is a choice. Change control exists because rollbacks are slower than confidence.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: ESD is quiet damage
domains.summary: ESD is quiet damage. You can kill a RAM stick without a spark you feel. A strap to ground (and a mat) is cheaper than a mystery POST.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: If it is not tagged, it is folklore
domains.summary: If it is not tagged, it is folklore. Asset tags, serials, and a location beat ‘the tall Dell near accounting’.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Beep codes are a language
domains.summary: Beep codes are a language. POST beeps (or Capslock blinks on some laptops) point at RAM, GPU, or board before an OS exists.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Image dim is not always a dead panel
domains.summary: Image dim is not always a dead panel. A faint image with a torch test often means backlight/inverter/LED driver, not a dead LCD.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Speed/duplex mismatch is a silent tax
domains.summary: Speed/duplex mismatch is a silent tax. One side 100/full, the other auto that fell to 100/half, equals collisions and sadness.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: IPv6 privacy addresses rotate on purpose
domains.summary: IPv6 privacy addresses rotate on purpose. Temporary IPv6 addresses change. That is privacy, not a flapping NIC.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: The log is older than the reboot
domains.summary: The log is older than the reboot. Event Viewer tells you the first error, not the last popup. Filter by time around the incident.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: gpupdate is not magic dust
domains.summary: gpupdate is not magic dust. Group Policy applies in order, with refresh intervals. A deny at the OU beats a hopeful gpupdate /force poem.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Reuse is the incident
domains.summary: Reuse is the incident. A unique password in a manager plus MFA beats a clever personal scheme reused on five SaaS boxes.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Guest Wi-Fi is a fence
domains.summary: Guest Wi-Fi is a fence. Client isolation and a separate SSID/VLAN stop visitors from scanning tills.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Daisy-chain needs the right DisplayPort
domains.summary: Daisy-chain needs the right DisplayPort. MST daisy-chain wants DP 1.2+ and a monitor that actually supports it. HDMI-in on the second panel is not a chain.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Swap one variable
domains.summary: Swap one variable. A known-good cable/PSU/RAM stick tests a theory. Swapping five parts at once writes a mystery novel.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Do not start at PEBKAC
domains.summary: Do not start at PEBKAC. Users lie by accident and also hardware fails. Ask what changed, reproduce, then talk about clicks.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: TRIM is for SSDs that the OS can see
domains.summary: TRIM is for SSDs that the OS can see. TRIM (discard) helps SSD garbage collection. A RAID card or USB bridge may swallow it.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: A proxy setting can look like a dead WAN
domains.summary: A proxy setting can look like a dead WAN. WPAD/PAC files and a stale proxy send browsers into a building that no longer exists.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Kerberos hates a wrong clock
domains.summary: Kerberos hates a wrong clock. If a PC is more than about five minutes off, domain logon and tickets fail in ways that look like ‘password wrong’.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Found USB is not free software
domains.summary: Found USB is not free software. Rubber-ducky and poisoned sticks still work on curiosity. Autorun is less eager now; humans are not.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Exclusive mode steals the device
domains.summary: Exclusive mode steals the device. An app in exclusive WASAPI/ASIO mode can make every other sound look like a broken driver.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: A photo is a document
domains.summary: A photo is a document. Rear cabling, error LEDs, and the serial plate photograph well. Future-you cannot remember the mess.

domains.subject: tech
domains.title: Clearing TPM can be a hostage situation
domains.summary: Clearing TPM can be a hostage situation. BitLocker keys live with TPM + PIN/startup key. Clearing TPM without recovery keys is how you invent a brick.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Tenths are not extra zeros
domains.summary: Tenths are not extra zeros. 0.3 is three tenths. 0.03 is three hundredths. The zero is a chair, not decoration.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Line up the points, not the left edges
domains.summary: Line up the points, not the left edges. Adding decimals is adding matching places. 3.4 + 0.25 wants tenths under tenths.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: 1/3 is not 0.3
domains.summary: 1/3 is not 0.3. 1/3 = 0.333… repeating. Cutting it to 0.3 is a round, and three of those do not make a whole.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Five rounds by a rule you state
domains.summary: Five rounds by a rule you state. Many school rules: 5 or more rounds away from 0 on that digit. Bankers’ rounding is different. State the rule before you fight.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Scientific notation is a sliding window
domains.summary: Scientific notation is a sliding window. 4.5 × 10³ is 4500. The 4.5 is the significand; the 10³ counts how many places the point moved.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Significant figures are honesty about a tool
domains.summary: Significant figures are honesty about a tool. A cheap ruler does not justify eight decimal places. Significant figures are a claim about precision, not a vibe.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Milli is a thousand slices
domains.summary: Milli is a thousand slices. milli- is 10⁻³, centi- 10⁻², kilo- 10³. 2.5 m = 2500 mm because you multiplied by 1000.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Minus is a direction on decimals too
domains.summary: Minus is a direction on decimals too. −0.4 is left of 0. It is smaller than −0.1. ‘Smaller’ on a number line is more left, not ‘closer to zero’.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Multiply, then park the point
domains.summary: Multiply, then park the point. 3.2 × 1.4: multiply 32 × 14, then the total decimal places (one + one = two) sit in the product.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Dividing by 0.1 makes it ten times bigger
domains.summary: Dividing by 0.1 makes it ten times bigger. ÷ 0.1 is × 10. A smaller divisor means more groups fit. 6 ÷ 0.1 = 60.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: A ratio is a recipe, not a pair of islands
domains.summary: A ratio is a recipe, not a pair of islands. 2:3 flour to water means 2 parts and 3 parts of the same size. Total parts = 5.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Per one is the honest comparison
domains.summary: Per one is the honest comparison. A unit rate is ‘for 1’. $4.80 per 12 means $0.40 each. Compare per 1 or per 100 g, not per bag.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Speed is a rate with a direction in time
domains.summary: Speed is a rate with a direction in time. average speed = distance / time. 120 km in 2 h is 60 km/h. It is not 120 km/h because the number 120 looks faster.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Density is stuff per space
domains.summary: Density is stuff per space. Population density is people per km². A huge empty shire can have fewer people per km² than a tiny suburb.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: 1:100 000 is a shrink, not a hint
domains.summary: 1:100 000 is a shrink, not a hint. 1 cm on the map is 100 000 cm in the world (1 km). Measure, then multiply by the scale.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: GST sits after the rate, unless the ticket says included
domains.summary: GST sits after the rate, unless the ticket says included. In Australia GST is 10%. ‘Plus GST’ means × 1.10 at the end. Unit price comparisons must use the same tax treatment.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: More workers can mean fewer hours
domains.summary: More workers can mean fewer hours. If the job is a fixed pile of work, twice the people can mean half the time (when they do not trip over each other).

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Percent change needs the old base
domains.summary: Percent change needs the old base. Increase 50 → 60 is +20% because 10/50 = 0.2. 60 → 50 is not −20% of 60 in the same breath without saying so.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Simple interest is a flat hire of money
domains.summary: Simple interest is a flat hire of money. I = Prt with r as a decimal. $1000 at 5% for 3 years simple is $150 interest, not $1500.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Compound interest is interest on the pile
domains.summary: Compound interest is interest on the pile. A = P(1+r)^n. 5% for 2 years on $1000 is 1000 × 1.05² = $1102.50, not $1100.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Like terms share the letters and powers
domains.summary: Like terms share the letters and powers. 3x and 5x add to 8x. 3x and 5x² do not. The power is part of the name.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: A minus outside the brackets flips signs
domains.summary: A minus outside the brackets flips signs. −(x − 4) = −x + 4. The minus is a −1 multiplying every term.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Do the same to both sides
domains.summary: Do the same to both sides. An equation is a balance. Subtract 3 from both sides, not from the side you dislike.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Multiply by a negative and the inequality flips
domains.summary: Multiply by a negative and the inequality flips. −2x > 6 → x < −3. The flip is the price of multiplying by a negative.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Gradient is rise over run
domains.summary: Gradient is rise over run. m = (y2−y1)/(x2−x1). A slope of 2 means up 2 for right 1. Negative is down as you go right.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: c is where it hits the y-axis
domains.summary: c is where it hits the y-axis. In y = mx + c, when x=0, y=c. That is the intercept, not a secret gradient.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Substitution is plug-in, then order
domains.summary: Substitution is plug-in, then order. If x=3 in 2x², that is 2×9=18, not (2×3)²=36 unless the brackets say so.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Factor out what every term actually shares
domains.summary: Factor out what every term actually shares. 6x + 9 = 3(2x+3). The 3 is in both. Do not invent an x in the 9.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: FOIL is just distribute twice
domains.summary: FOIL is just distribute twice. (x+2)(x+3)=x²+5x+6. Each term in the first bracket meets each in the second.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Same base: add the indices when multiplying
domains.summary: Same base: add the indices when multiplying. a³ × a² = a⁵. You are counting factors of a, not multiplying the little numbers for sport.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: a⁰ is 1 (if a is not 0)
domains.summary: a⁰ is 1 (if a is not 0). The empty product is 1. a³/a³=a⁰=1. 0⁰ is a fight you should not pick in this path.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: An arithmetic sequence adds the same each time
domains.summary: An arithmetic sequence adds the same each time. 3, 7, 11, 15 … common difference +4. Term n is first + (n−1)d.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: A straight line is 180°
domains.summary: A straight line is 180°. Adjacent angles on a straight line add to 180°. A ‘straight-looking’ drawing is not a proof without that fact or a given.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: A triangle owns 180°
domains.summary: A triangle owns 180°. Interior angles of a triangle add to 180°, Euclidean and flat. A 90° corner leaves 90° for the other two to share.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Pythagoras wants a right angle
domains.summary: Pythagoras wants a right angle. a²+b²=c² only for right triangles, c the hypotenuse (longest, opposite 90°).

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Area is length × length
domains.summary: Area is length × length. m × m = m². A 3 m by 4 m rectangle is 12 m², not 12 m, not 7 m.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: π is circumference over diameter
domains.summary: π is circumference over diameter. C=πd=2πr. Area=πr². Mixing them is the national sport.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Similar means same shape, scaled
domains.summary: Similar means same shape, scaled. Equal angles, sides in proportion. A 2× scale multiplies lengths by 2 and areas by 4.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: A prism is a base I can slide
domains.summary: A prism is a base I can slide. Volume of a prism = base area × height (the slide). A triangular prism uses triangle area, not ‘three rectangles and hope’.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: A net is the skin unfolded
domains.summary: A net is the skin unfolded. Surface area is the sum of the faces. A net that overlaps or misses a face will lie.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: A bearing is from north, clockwise
domains.summary: A bearing is from north, clockwise. 035° is 35° east of north. Three digits. It is not an angle inside a random triangle unless you draw north.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Midpoint averages the coordinates
domains.summary: Midpoint averages the coordinates. M = ((x1+x2)/2, (y1+y2)/2). It is the average of positions, not the average of the distances as a vibe.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: A translation is a slide, not a stretch
domains.summary: A translation is a slide, not a stretch. Vector (3,−2) means +3 x, −2 y. Shape, size, angles stay. It is not a scale.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: The mean is a fair share; the median is the middle
domains.summary: The mean is a fair share; the median is the middle. Mean = total / count. Median = middle of an ordered list. An outlier yanks the mean harder.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Range is a blunt spread
domains.summary: Range is a blunt spread. Range = max − min. Two classes can share a mean and not share a range.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: A bar chart is categories; a histogram is bins
domains.summary: A bar chart is categories; a histogram is bins. Bars for colours of cars can have gaps. Histograms for heights glue bins; area (not just height) can carry frequency.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Probability lives between 0 and 1
domains.summary: Probability lives between 0 and 1. 0 is impossible, 1 is certain. 0.2 is 1 in 5, or 20%. 120% as a probability is a marketing leak.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Independent AND multiplies
domains.summary: Independent AND multiplies. P(two heads in a row) on a fair coin = 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4, if flips do not care about each other.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: OR for disjoint events adds
domains.summary: OR for disjoint events adds. P(heart or spade) = 13/52 + 13/52 = 1/2. You cannot draw both from one card.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Who you asked is the result
domains.summary: Who you asked is the result. A survey at a tram stop at 2 am is not ‘Australians’. Bias is a sampling story, not a rude word.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: An outlier is a suspect, not a delete key
domains.summary: An outlier is a suspect, not a delete key. A point far from the pack may be a typing error (5.0 vs 50) or a real rare event. You need a reason to drop it.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: A two-way table is a cross of categories
domains.summary: A two-way table is a cross of categories. Rows one variable, columns the other. Totals on the edges. Conditional probability is a row (or column) as the new whole.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Expected value is a long-run average
domains.summary: Expected value is a long-run average. E = sum of (value × probability). A $10 raffle with 1/100 of $200 has E=$2, so $10 is a donation if you wanted the mean.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Correlation is not a boss of causation
domains.summary: Correlation is not a boss of causation. Points trending up together are associated. Ice cream and drowning both rise in summer; heat is the lurking variable.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: Roots are where the parabola kisses the x-axis
domains.summary: Roots are where the parabola kisses the x-axis. Solutions of y=x²−5x+6 are x=2 and x=3 because (x−2)(x−3)=0. They are x-intercepts, not the vertex automatically.

domains.subject: maths
domains.title: A box plot is a five-number story
domains.summary: A box plot is a five-number story. Min, Q1, median, Q3, max. IQR = Q3−Q1 is the middle half. Whiskers are not error bars from a lab.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: A group is a family of habits
domains.summary: A group is a family of habits. Columns share valence patterns. Alkali metals (group 1) get more reactive down the column; noble gases mostly do not form everyday compounds.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: A phase change is not a new substance
domains.summary: A phase change is not a new substance. Melting ice is H2O(s) → H2O(l). Same molecules, different arrangement. Burning methane makes new molecules.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Atoms are not created in a beaker
domains.summary: Atoms are not created in a beaker. A closed rusting jar gains no magic mass from nowhere; oxygen from the air joins the iron. Open-air rust looks heavier because of that join.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: pH 3 is not ‘a bit more than 4’
domains.summary: pH 3 is not ‘a bit more than 4’. pH is logarithmic. Each whole number is a ten-times change in H+ concentration. pH 3 is ten times more acidic than pH 4.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: A mixture keeps the recipes of its parts
domains.summary: A mixture keeps the recipes of its parts. Air is a mixture; water is a compound. You can (in principle) sieve or distill a mixture without breaking molecules.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Endothermic does not mean ‘cold forever’
domains.summary: Endothermic does not mean ‘cold forever’. An endothermic change takes energy in (photosynthesis, some instant ice packs). The surroundings can feel cooler while the system stores.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: A catalyst is a cheaper door, not a free lunch
domains.summary: A catalyst is a cheaper door, not a free lunch. Catalysts lower activation energy and are not used up as a net reactant. They do not change the energy difference between start.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Isotopes share protons, not neutrons
domains.summary: Isotopes share protons, not neutrons. Carbon-12 and carbon-14 both have 6 protons. 14 has two extra neutrons. Chemistry is mostly the proton count; mass and stability can differ.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Ionic is a steal; covalent is a share
domains.summary: Ionic is a steal; covalent is a share. Metal + non-metal often ionise (NaCl). Two non-metals often share (O2, H2O). The bond name is a model, not a moral.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Concentration is amount per volume
domains.summary: Concentration is amount per volume. A darker cordial can be more concentrated, or just a deeper glass. mol/L or g/L is the honest unit.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Seasons are a tilt, not a closer hug
domains.summary: Seasons are a tilt, not a closer hug. Earth is slightly closer to the Sun in a southern summer? Actually perihelion is early January — so distance is the wrong story. Tilt.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Day and night are a spin
domains.summary: Day and night are a spin. Earth rotates about its axis in about 24 h. The Sun ‘rises’ because we turn, not because the Sun orbits us daily.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Phases are a lighting angle, not a bite
domains.summary: Phases are a lighting angle, not a bite. We see the half of the Moon that faces the Sun. The ‘crescent’ is that lighting from our seat, not Earth’s shadow (that would be an.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Plates do not care about country borders
domains.summary: Plates do not care about country borders. Earthquakes cluster at plate edges: diverge, converge, slide. Australia sits mid-plate, so big quakes are rarer — not impossible.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Rocks are recipes that can be remade
domains.summary: Rocks are recipes that can be remade. Igneous from melt, sedimentary from bits, metamorphic from heat/pressure. The cycle is paths, not a one-way career.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: The water cycle is the same water on tour
domains.summary: The water cycle is the same water on tour. Evaporation, condensation, precipitation, runoff/infiltration. Energy from the Sun lifts water; gravity brings it back.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Greenhouse gases are a blanket, not a window tax
domains.summary: Greenhouse gases are a blanket, not a window tax. CO2, methane, water vapour let visible light in and hold some infrared on the way out. More blanket, more stored heat.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Ozone holes are not the same dial as climate
domains.summary: Ozone holes are not the same dial as climate. Stratospheric ozone absorbs UV. CFCs punched a hole. That is a different molecule story from CO2’s infrared blanket.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Stars are fusion engines, not campfires
domains.summary: Stars are fusion engines, not campfires. Hydrogen nuclei fuse to helium in main-sequence stars, releasing energy (E=mc² neighbourhood). A campfire is a chemical rearrange.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Orbits are mostly empty
domains.summary: Orbits are mostly empty. A classroom-scale Sun the size of a melon puts Earth a long walk away and Neptune off the oval. Posters squash space.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Weathering breaks; erosion moves
domains.summary: Weathering breaks; erosion moves. Weathering is the breakdown in place. Erosion is the taxi (water, wind, ice, gravity). A cliff can weather for years before a slump erodes it.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Fossils keep a sedimentary diary
domains.summary: Fossils keep a sedimentary diary. Hard parts and traces bury in sediment that lithifies. Granite will not keep a fern the same way.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Humans run a double loop
domains.summary: Humans run a double loop. Pulmonary circuit: heart → lungs → heart. Systemic: heart → body → heart. Oxygen pick-up and delivery are different errands.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Alveoli are the exchange rooms
domains.summary: Alveoli are the exchange rooms. Thin walls, huge surface area, capillaries next door. O2 in, CO2 out by diffusion — high to low concentration.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Digestion is disassembly; absorption is the pickup
domains.summary: Digestion is disassembly; absorption is the pickup. Enzymes cut polymers to small bits. The small intestine’s villi pick them up. A long tube is not enough without the chemistry.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: A neuron is a one-way wire with chemistry at the gap
domains.summary: A neuron is a one-way wire with chemistry at the gap. Electrical along the axon, chemical across the synapse. The next cell has to have receptors. It is not copper.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Immunity is a self/not-self argument
domains.summary: Immunity is a self/not-self argument. White cells and antibodies tag non-self. Vaccines show a safe preview so memory cells wait. Autoimmune is the argument going wrong.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Homeostasis is a thermostat, not a freeze-frame
domains.summary: Homeostasis is a thermostat, not a freeze-frame. Blood sugar, temperature, water: sensors, control, effectors. Negative feedback turns the response down as you near the set point.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Bones are levers; joints are the hinges
domains.summary: Bones are levers; joints are the hinges. Muscles pull (they do not push). Antagonistic pairs (biceps/triceps) because a pull needs a partner to go the other way.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: An allele is a version, not a whole extra gene
domains.summary: An allele is a version, not a whole extra gene. You inherit two copies of most genes (one from each parent). Dominant/recessive is about how they show, not ‘stronger person’.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: A virus is not a cell on a diet
domains.summary: A virus is not a cell on a diet. Viruses need a host to copy. They have genetic material and a coat, not a full metabolism. Antibiotics miss them.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Skin is an organ with a job
domains.summary: Skin is an organ with a job. Barrier, vitamin D factory (with UV), temperature control, sensors. A cut is a broken wall, not just a cosmetic line.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Kidneys filter, then reclaim
domains.summary: Kidneys filter, then reclaim. Nephrons filter blood, then take back water and useful solutes. Urine is the leftovers plus what you needed to dump (urea).

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Metals conduct heat because electrons wander
domains.summary: Metals conduct heat because electrons wander. Delocalised electrons carry energy through a pan. Wood does not, which is why handles exist.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: A circuit is a loop, not a hose that empties
domains.summary: A circuit is a loop, not a hose that empties. Current is a flow of charge. Voltage is the push. Resistance makes it harder. A break anywhere stops a series loop.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Poles come in pairs; field lines are a map
domains.summary: Poles come in pairs; field lines are a map. Cut a magnet and you get two smaller magnets, not a lonely north. Field lines leave north and enter south by convention.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Sound needs a medium; light does not
domains.summary: Sound needs a medium; light does not. Sound is a vibration through matter. No air, no chat (space films that boom are lying). Light is an electromagnetic wave and can cross vacuum.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Angle in equals angle out
domains.summary: Angle in equals angle out. On a mirror, measured from the normal (the perpendicular). A rough wall scatters; a lake can glare.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Photosynthesis banks light as sugar
domains.summary: Photosynthesis banks light as sugar. CO2 + water + light → glucose + oxygen (in the school equation). It stores energy; respiration in cells spends it.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Food energy is joules (or Calories) from bonds
domains.summary: Food energy is joules (or Calories) from bonds. Respiration releases energy from glucose. A label’s kJ is a bomb-calorimeter neighbourhood, not ‘how tired you feel’.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Renewable is a source story; dispatchable is a timing story
domains.summary: Renewable is a source story; dispatchable is a timing story. Solar and wind are renewable and variable. Hydro and batteries help time-shift. ‘Baseload’ is a grid-behaviour word,.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Classification is a nested filing cabinet
domains.summary: Classification is a nested filing cabinet. Domain → … → genus → species. A species name is binomial (Homo sapiens). It is a hypothesis about relatedness, updated with evidence.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: A web is arrows of energy, not friendship
domains.summary: A web is arrows of energy, not friendship. Arrows point to the eater (energy to the consumer). Knock out a node and the effects branch. A chain is a simplified path through a web.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: An adaptation is a heritable fit, not a wish
domains.summary: An adaptation is a heritable fit, not a wish. Thick leaves in a banksiadry heath are a selected trait over generations. One thirsty plant does not ‘decide’ to grow thicker leaves.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Carbon walks between air and bodies
domains.summary: Carbon walks between air and bodies. Photosynthesis pulls CO2 in; respiration and burning push it out. A forest is a stock; a fire is a flux.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Most microbes are not villains
domains.summary: Most microbes are not villains. Nitrogen fixers, gut communities, decomposers. Pathogens are the famous minority. Sterile is not always safer.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: A river can look clean and still be sick
domains.summary: A river can look clean and still be sick. Dissolved oxygen, turbidity, nutrients, macroinvertebrates. Algal blooms after fertiliser are a nutrient story, not a ‘green means.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Introduced is about the ecosystem, not a passport stamp
domains.summary: Introduced is about the ecosystem, not a passport stamp. Rabbits, cane toads, lantana: they win because controls that held them at home are missing. Native can still be pests in.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Fire is a regime, not a single match
domains.summary: Fire is a regime, not a single match. Frequency, intensity, season. Some Australian plants need smoke or heat to germinate. Too often, or too hot, still wrecks the script.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Mitosis copies; meiosis shuffles
domains.summary: Mitosis copies; meiosis shuffles. Mitosis: two same-ish body cells. Meiosis: gametes with half the chromosomes and new mixes. That is why kids are not clones.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: A tropism is a plant’s slow reply
domains.summary: A tropism is a plant’s slow reply. Phototropism: grow toward light (auxin story). Not a brain. Still a stimulus–response chain.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Diversity is more than a species count
domains.summary: Diversity is more than a species count. Richness (how many kinds) and evenness (how stacked). A plantation of one tree can be green and poor.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Pressure in a gas is collisions on a wall
domains.summary: Pressure in a gas is collisions on a wall. More particles, more speed (temperature), or less volume → more hits. A bike pump heats because you did work on the gas.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Tides are a two-bulge story
domains.summary: Tides are a two-bulge story. The Moon’s gravity plus Earth’s motion make two tidal bulges. The Sun joins in (spring/neap). Spinning Earth under the bulges makes the rhythm.

domains.subject: science
domains.title: Efficiency is useful out over total in
domains.summary: Efficiency is useful out over total in. A 40% efficient motor dumps 60% as heat and sound. Perpetual motion would need 100% plus a gift.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: A primary source was there
domains.summary: A primary source was there. A letter from 1854 is primary for that event. A textbook chapter is secondary. A memoir written fifty years later is primary for memory, slippery for.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Bias is a lean, not a swear
domains.summary: Bias is a lean, not a swear. Every source has a seat: who paid, who was scared, who wanted a vote. Naming the lean is the skill. ‘Biased so useless’ is a cop-out.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Causes stack; they are not a single villain
domains.summary: Causes stack; they are not a single villain. Long-term fuel, short-term spark, and choices in the room. ‘Because of one person’ is a movie, sometimes a factor, rarely the whole.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Do not send them your phone
domains.summary: Do not send them your phone. Judging 1800s people as if they had your newsfeed is anachronism. You can still judge cruelty; you must not fake their options.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The archive has holes on purpose and by accident
domains.summary: The archive has holes on purpose and by accident. Who could write, whose papers were kept, whose language the clerk spoke. Silence is evidence of power, not proof that nothing.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: One source is a claim; two is a conversation
domains.summary: One source is a claim; two is a conversation. Corroboration is overlap plus friction. If they agree word-for-word, one might have copied. If they fight, you just got a lead.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Periods are boxes we made
domains.summary: Periods are boxes we made. ‘The 1960s’ did not start on 1 January for everyone. Periods help teaching; they hide overlap and people who missed the memo.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Historical empathy is reconstructing a world, not blessing it
domains.summary: Historical empathy is reconstructing a world, not blessing it. You try to see their constraints. You do not have to like the constraints. Empathy is a method; endorsement is a.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The Nile’s gift was a calendar
domains.summary: The Nile’s gift was a calendar. Predictable floods laid silt; priests and administrators made a state that could tax grain. Geography did not ‘cause’ pyramids by itself — people.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Athenian democracy had a guest list
domains.summary: Athenian democracy had a guest list. Citizen men voted. Women, enslaved people, and metics did not. The word ‘democracy’ is not a sticker you slap on the whole city.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Roads were a military app
domains.summary: Roads were a military app. Rome built paths for legions and tax. Trade rode along. The road is not a gift shop; it is logistics.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Han China bet on clerks
domains.summary: Han China bet on clerks. Recommendation and later examination cultures tried to staff an empire with literate officials. It was never purely merit — pedigree still talked.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The Silk Road was many roads
domains.summary: The Silk Road was many roads. Goods, Buddhists, diseases, and stories. ‘Silk’ is a nickname. Oasis towns taxed the caravans; empires tried to own the tax.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Translation was a power move
domains.summary: Translation was a power move. Baghdad’s House of Wisdom stories (and other cities) gathered Greek, Persian, Indian science into Arabic. Europe later borrowed. Knowledge had visas.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The Mongol moment was violence and a post office
domains.summary: The Mongol moment was violence and a post office. Conquest, massacre, and also a Pax that moved merchants and plague. Both sentences can be true. Cheerleading is optional.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Print multiplied arguments
domains.summary: Print multiplied arguments. Movable type in Europe (and earlier print cultures in East Asia) changed who could afford a pamphlet. Reformation and rumour both scaled.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: 1492 shuffled living things
domains.summary: 1492 shuffled living things. Potatoes, maize, horses, smallpox. Calorie maps and death maps moved. It was not ‘discovering empty land’.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The Atlantic system was a machine
domains.summary: The Atlantic system was a machine. Captives, Middle Passage, plantations, sugar/cotton profits, and laws that made people into property. It was not a series of unfortunate.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Coal plus mills rewrote time
domains.summary: Coal plus mills rewrote time. Steam, factories, child labour, and a new clock. Rural putting-out died unevenly. Smoke was a class experience.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: 1789 was a stack that slipped
domains.summary: 1789 was a stack that slipped. Debt, bad harvests, Enlightenment talk, and a king who ran out of road. Terror and Napoleon were sequels, not proofs that the first demand was fake.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Meiji Japan chose a crash course
domains.summary: Meiji Japan chose a crash course. Faced with gunboat power, reformers abolished the old order fast: industry, army, constitution with a catch. It was not ‘Westernisation’ as.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The Western Front was industrial killing
domains.summary: The Western Front was industrial killing. Artillery, mud, and a state that could feed the guns. ‘Lions led by donkeys’ is a debate, not a caption you skip evidence for.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Total war ate the home street
domains.summary: Total war ate the home street. Rationing, bombing, women’s labour, internment. The ‘front’ was also a factory and a kitchen. Propaganda was a tool, not wallpaper.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The Cold War was hot in other people’s countries
domains.summary: The Cold War was hot in other people’s countries. Nuclear stalemate in the centres, wars and coups at the edges. ‘Peace’ in Europe could be war in Korea, Vietnam, or Afghanistan.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Flags changed; strings often did not
domains.summary: Flags changed; strings often did not. After 1945 many empires folded under cost, war, and nationalist movements. Borders could be hasty. Neo-colonial economics could stay.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: This continent has deep human time
domains.summary: This continent has deep human time. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples’ occupancy is tens of thousands of years — among the longest continuous cultures. ‘Prehistory’.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Songlines are knowledge systems
domains.summary: Songlines are knowledge systems. Routes, law, and land are braided in ceremony and story. They are not ‘myths for kids’ in the dismissive sense. They are maps with obligations.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Terra nullius was a legal story that failed
domains.summary: Terra nullius was a legal story that failed. The claim of land belonging to no one ignored law, farming, and presence. Mabo (1992) killed it in Australian law; the political.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The frontier was not a handshake
domains.summary: The frontier was not a handshake. Violence, disease, and resistance. ‘Settlement’ can be accurate as a government word and still hide killings. Historians argue scale; they do.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Gold scrambled the colonies
domains.summary: Gold scrambled the colonies. Population spike, Eureka, anti-Chinese riots, and a more assertive colonial politics. Gold is a mineral and a social bomb.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Federation was a deal, not a destiny
domains.summary: Federation was a deal, not a destiny. Defence fears, tariffs, railways of different gauges, and a White Australia consensus. Women and Indigenous people were not equally in the.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: White Australia was policy, not mood
domains.summary: White Australia was policy, not mood. Dictation tests and later variants tried to control who could come. It was popular in its day and is a stain you should name, not mumble.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Anzac is memory with politics
domains.summary: Anzac is memory with politics. Gallipoli was a failed campaign with courage and waste. The legend was built in newspapers, schools, and later governments. You can honour dead.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The Depression was a dole and a riot
domains.summary: The Depression was a dole and a riot. Unemployment, eviction, Premiers’ Plan fights, and a generation that distrusted banks. Australia’s version had its own politics (Lang, Lyons).

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Populate or perish had a passenger list
domains.summary: Populate or perish had a passenger list. Displaced Europeans, then later sources, rebuilt labour and cities. ‘New Australian’ was a phrase with a pecking order. First Nations.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: 1967 was a count, not a magic wand
domains.summary: 1967 was a count, not a magic wand. The referendum let the Commonwealth count Aboriginal people in the census and make laws. It did not grant a wage, land, or an apology by itself.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Removal was a policy with files
domains.summary: Removal was a policy with files. Children taken under ‘protection’ and assimilation. Bringing Them Home (1997) collected testimony. The Apology (2008) was a speech, not a time.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Mabo was a court fight on a reef of law
domains.summary: Mabo was a court fight on a reef of law. Eddie Mabo and others proved Meriam law on Mer. Native title is recognised where it survived, with extinguishment rules that bite.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: 1999 was a model fight, not only a crown fight
domains.summary: 1999 was a model fight, not only a crown fight. Voters were asked about a specific republic design. Many who disliked the model voted no without loving the monarchy. Process was.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Some Australian women voted early — not all
domains.summary: Some Australian women voted early — not all. White women got federal votes early compared with much of the world. Aboriginal women (and men) were often excluded in practice and.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The eight-hour day was a fight
domains.summary: The eight-hour day was a fight. Stonemasons in the 1850s and later unions pushed 8-8-8. Leisure was political. It did not arrive as a gift from a kind factory.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The pension was an argument about who deserves
domains.summary: The pension was an argument about who deserves. Age pensions, invalidity, later unemployment insurance — each had a moral test. Indigenous access was often delayed or denied.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Newspapers made publics
domains.summary: Newspapers made publics. Partisan papers, later broadcasting, now platforms. A ‘public’ is assembled, not found under a rock. Censorship in war is a recurring tool.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Teenagers were invented as a market and a panic
domains.summary: Teenagers were invented as a market and a panic. Postwar wages, rock’n’roll, and moral panics. Youth culture is not trivial — it is consumption, identity, and policing.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Green bans were labour plus ecology
domains.summary: Green bans were labour plus ecology. NSW builders’ labourers refused work on some sites (Kelly’s Bush and others). Heritage and class met on a scaffold.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Decriminalisation was a calendar of states
domains.summary: Decriminalisation was a calendar of states. Homosexuality laws fell at different speeds in different Australian jurisdictions. The Sydney Mardi Gras began as a protest, not a.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Access is a political demand
domains.summary: Access is a political demand. Institutions, then deinstitutionalisation fights, then DDA-style law. A ramp is a policy, not a courtesy.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: A museum is an argument in glass
domains.summary: A museum is an argument in glass. What is displayed, what is repatriated, whose voice is on the label. Objectivity is a tone, not a fact of the building.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Memory is a source with weather
domains.summary: Memory is a source with weather. Interview a person and you get meaning, emotion, and drift. That can be more true about experience than a shipping list, and worse about a date.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: A map is a claim on paper
domains.summary: A map is a claim on paper. Borders, names, empty interiors. Colonial maps can erase paths that existed. A Mercator classroom map stretches power.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: A census is a power tool
domains.summary: A census is a power tool. Who is counted, as what, by whom. 1967 changed a count. Categories (race, occupation) are historical, not natural kinds.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: A statue is a sentence in bronze
domains.summary: A statue is a sentence in bronze. Who paid, when it went up, who is not on the plinth. Taking one down is also a historical event, not only a tantrum.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Digitised is not complete
domains.summary: Digitised is not complete. Search boxes love print and English. Handwriting, off-digitised series, and paywalls still hide. OCR misreads names.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: The Ottoman end redrew a map with a ruler
domains.summary: The Ottoman end redrew a map with a ruler. WWI killed an empire. Mandates, new states, and promises that conflicted (including over Palestine) are the hangover. ‘Artificial.

domains.subject: history
domains.title: Australia’s Vietnam was an alliance choice
domains.summary: Australia’s Vietnam was an alliance choice. Forward defence, conscription ballot, moratoriums. Veterans’ return was not a single parade feeling. The war’s meaning split the street.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A sentence needs a complete job
domains.summary: A sentence needs a complete job. A finite verb and a subject doing something (or being something) usually make a clause that can stand. ‘Because the bus’ is a fragment.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A comma cannot weld two sentences
domains.summary: A comma cannot weld two sentences. ‘The bell rang, we ran’ is a splice. You want a full stop, a semicolon, or a joining word.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A run-on is a pile-up, not enthusiasm
domains.summary: A run-on is a pile-up, not enthusiasm. Two or more main clauses with no legal join. Excitement is not a conjunction.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: The verb agrees with the subject, not the nearest noun
domains.summary: The verb agrees with the subject, not the nearest noun. ‘The box of biscuits is’ — box is singular. ‘Biscuits’ is a decoy.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Pick a time and stay unless you mean to jump
domains.summary: Pick a time and stay unless you mean to jump. A recount that hops past/present without a reason feels like a glitch, not a voice.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Passive hides the doer — sometimes on purpose
domains.summary: Passive hides the doer — sometimes on purpose. ‘The window was broken’ vs ‘Sam broke the window’. Science methods use passive to focus on the procedure; politics uses it to dodge.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A dangling modifier attaches to the wrong head
domains.summary: A dangling modifier attaches to the wrong head. ‘Running for the bus, the backpack bounced’ — the backpack was not running.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Lists want the same grammatical clothes
domains.summary: Lists want the same grammatical clothes. ‘She likes hiking, to swim, and bicycles’ is a jumble. Make them all -ing, or all nouns, or all clauses.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A colon introduces a payoff you already set up
domains.summary: A colon introduces a payoff you already set up. A complete clause, then a colon, then the list or the reveal. Do not colon after ‘such as’ as a reflex.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Apostrophes are ownership or missing letters, not extras
domains.summary: Apostrophes are ownership or missing letters, not extras. cat’s = of the cat (or cat is). cats = more than one cat. cats’ = of the cats. Its = belonging to it; it’s = it is.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A semicolon joins cousins, not strangers
domains.summary: A semicolon joins cousins, not strangers. Two complete sentences that belong together: ‘The bus was late; we still made the bell.’

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A subordinate clause cannot stand alone
domains.summary: A subordinate clause cannot stand alone. ‘Although it rained’ wants a main clause. That is a dependent thought.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Inference is a trace plus a because
domains.summary: Inference is a trace plus a because. The text does not say ‘she is angry’; the slammed locker and short answers do. You still need the evidence line.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: The main idea is the spine, not the first sentence always
domains.summary: The main idea is the spine, not the first sentence always. Topic sentences help. Sometimes the spine is delayed. Details decorate; they are not the claim.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A fact can be checked; an opinion is a stance
domains.summary: A fact can be checked; an opinion is a stance. ‘The hall holds 400’ vs ‘the hall is ugly’. Loaded words can smuggle opinion into a fact-shaped line.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Who is this for, and what is it trying to do
domains.summary: Who is this for, and what is it trying to do. A Year 4 safety poster and a senate submission can share a topic and not share a voice. Audience plus purpose choose the features.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Tone is the attitude in the word choices
domains.summary: Tone is the attitude in the word choices. Sarcastic, solemn, matey. Not the plot. A funeral speech in meme-speak is a tone crash unless that is the point.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A shift is a door in the text
domains.summary: A shift is a door in the text. A volta in a sonnet, a ‘but’ paragraph, a cut in a film. Structure is not a box-tick of intro-body-conclusion only.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Comparison wants a lens, not two summaries glued
domains.summary: Comparison wants a lens, not two summaries glued. Both texts, one idea: how they treat power, or endings, or a symbol. A+B summaries is two book reports.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Context is the world around the text, not a Wikipedia dump
domains.summary: Context is the world around the text, not a Wikipedia dump. A wartime ration book next to a poem about cake. Use what changes the reading, then return to the words.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: An unreliable narrator is a designed leak
domains.summary: An unreliable narrator is a designed leak. They omit, boast, or fail to see. You catch them via other clues in the text, not via ‘I didn’t like them’.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Images have grammar too
domains.summary: Images have grammar too. Salience, vectors, colour, framing, demand vs offer gaze. A poster is not ‘just a picture’.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Enjambment is a run-on that is on purpose
domains.summary: Enjambment is a run-on that is on purpose. The sentence keeps going over the line break. The break is a breath or a trap, not a mistake.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A topic is a noun; a theme is a claim about it
domains.summary: A topic is a noun; a theme is a claim about it. Topic: friendship. Theme: friendship can be a cover for control. If you only name the topic, you have not started.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A thesis is a contestable sentence
domains.summary: A thesis is a contestable sentence. It can be disagreed with. ‘This essay will discuss sharks’ is a table of contents, not a thesis.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A body paragraph needs a job-one line
domains.summary: A body paragraph needs a job-one line. The first sentence should say what this chunk proves. Quotes then work. A quote dump is not a paragraph.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A quotation is a passenger in your sentence
domains.summary: A quotation is a passenger in your sentence. Lead in, snip what you need, punctuate. A floating quote is a brick in the road.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: One paragraph, one job
domains.summary: One paragraph, one job. If you wander into a new claim, break. White space is a tool.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Cut the throat-clearing
domains.summary: Cut the throat-clearing. ‘In today’s society in this essay I will attempt to’ is fog. Start the claim.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Register is the clothing of the situation
domains.summary: Register is the clothing of the situation. A job email is not a snapchat. Slang can be precise in fiction and sloppy in a report.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Show is sensory and action; tell is a label
domains.summary: Show is sensory and action; tell is a label. ‘She was angry’ tells. A slammed locker can show. You still need tell sometimes (time jumps, inner rules).

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Dialogue punctuation is a small machine
domains.summary: Dialogue punctuation is a small machine. New speaker, new line. Commas inside the quote when the tag follows, in standard school style.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A plan is cheaper than a rewrite
domains.summary: A plan is cheaper than a rewrite. Five bullets of claims beat a beautiful first sentence that leads nowhere.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Editing is a different hat from drafting
domains.summary: Editing is a different hat from drafting. Draft for ideas. Edit for sense, then for sentences, then for ticks (spelling, quotes). One pass cannot do all jobs well.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Credit is a trail, not a decoration
domains.summary: Credit is a trail, not a decoration. Quote, paraphrase, and the idea you did not invent all want a trail. School styles (Harvard, APA) are machines — pick one.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Connotation is the cloud around a word
domains.summary: Connotation is the cloud around a word. Slim vs skinny vs scrawny. Denotation overlaps; the cloud does not. Propaganda lives in the cloud.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Turning a verb into a noun packs and hides
domains.summary: Turning a verb into a noun packs and hides. ‘They decided’ → ‘the decision’. Useful in reports; foggy when nobody is left to blame.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Metaphor says this is that; simile says like
domains.summary: Metaphor says this is that; simile says like. A metaphor does not need like/as. If every image is decorated, none land. Mixed metaphors (a storm that also has brakes) stall.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Modality is how sure the sentence is
domains.summary: Modality is how sure the sentence is. Must, might, could, will. High modality sounds certain. Low leaves room. A recipe wants high; a hypothesis may want low.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Cohesion is the glue: pronouns, synonyms, connectives
domains.summary: Cohesion is the glue: pronouns, synonyms, connectives. ‘This’ needs a clear noun nearby. Vague ‘this’ is a fog machine. Connectives should match the logic (but vs therefore).

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Roots are a map, not a spell
domains.summary: Roots are a map, not a spell. bio = life, graph = write. They help guesses. English still steals and lies (a pineapple is not a pine or an apple in the obvious way).

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Formal is precise, not just longer
domains.summary: Formal is precise, not just longer. Buy vs purchase. Sometimes purchase is right (a contract). Sometimes you just bought milk.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Ambiguity can be a bug or a feature
domains.summary: Ambiguity can be a bug or a feature. ‘The teacher hit the student with the book’ — who held the book? Grammar can fork. Poetry may want the fork; instructions must not.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Idioms are not Lego
domains.summary: Idioms are not Lego. ‘Kick the bucket’ is death, not sport. Learners (and literal robots) trip. Mix an idiom and you get sludge (‘we’ll burn that bridge when we come to it’).

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Spelling is patterns plus a few outlaws
domains.summary: Spelling is patterns plus a few outlaws. Hope → hoping (drop e). Hop → hopping (double). ‘I before e’ has a street of exceptions. Morphology (un- + happy) is more reliable than a.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Ethos is ‘why listen to me’
domains.summary: Ethos is ‘why listen to me’. Credentials, fairness, calm. It can be honest or costume. A white coat in an ad is often costume.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Pathos is a feeling on purpose
domains.summary: Pathos is a feeling on purpose. A sick child in a campaign, a joke in a speech. Feeling is not fake by default; it is a tool. Check what it is trying to make you do.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Logos is the reasoning chain
domains.summary: Logos is the reasoning chain. Data, examples, if-then. A number can still be cherry-picked. Logos is the chain, not ‘there was a graph’.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A speech lives in breath and time
domains.summary: A speech lives in breath and time. Short sentences, a pause, a repeat. What looks repetitive on a page can land in a hall. What looks clever on a page can die in a mumble.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Audio has no italics — the voice does the work
domains.summary: Audio has no italics — the voice does the work. Pace, music stings, who gets the last word in an edit. A transcript misses the smirk.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: An ad is a targeting machine
domains.summary: An ad is a targeting machine. Audience slice, problem, product as hero, tiny print. Representation (who is shown) is a claim about who matters.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A news angle is a choice of front door
domains.summary: A news angle is a choice of front door. Same event: ‘chaos’ vs ‘families wait’. Headline, photo, and lead sentence pick a door. Objectivity is a set of habits, not a halo.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A caption is a frame, not a sticker
domains.summary: A caption is a frame, not a sticker. The same image with ‘hero’ vs ‘hoarder’ trains the eye. Alt-text is access and also a frame.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A stereotype is a shortcut that costs someone
domains.summary: A stereotype is a shortcut that costs someone. Stock characters (the nag, the thug) travel because they are cheap. Critique is naming the shortcut and who it harms.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Texts talk to other texts
domains.summary: Texts talk to other texts. An allusion, a remix, a genre template. You only hear it if you know the other text — or the new one teaches you.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A pitch has an order that does work
domains.summary: A pitch has an order that does work. Hook, problem, proof, answer, ask. Skipping the ask is a speech that claps itself.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: People are not their labels as a whole self
domains.summary: People are not their labels as a whole self. Person-first or identity-first depends on communities (many Autistic advocates prefer identity-first). The skill is following the.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: An introduction earns the next line
domains.summary: An introduction earns the next line. A hook that is a question dumped from a list (‘Have you ever thought about themes?’) is a groan. Better: a precise tension from the text.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: A conclusion is a last turn, not a copy-paste
domains.summary: A conclusion is a last turn, not a copy-paste. Synthesise (so what, who cares) rather than reprint paragraph one. No new giant claim that needed evidence.

domains.subject: english
domains.title: Satire attacks with a grin that has teeth
domains.summary: Satire attacks with a grin that has teeth. It imitates to expose. If the reader thinks the mask is the face, satire failed (or they did). Modest Proposal is the nuclear example.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Latitude is the ladder, longitude the doors
domains.summary: Latitude is the ladder, longitude the doors. Latitude measures north–south from the equator. Longitude measures east–west from Greenwich. Together they are an address, not a vibe.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Map scale is a shrink factor
domains.summary: Map scale is a shrink factor. 1:100 000 means 1 cm on the map is 1 km on the ground. Measure, then multiply. ‘Large scale’ means more detail, not a bigger number on the right of.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Every flat map lies somewhere
domains.summary: Every flat map lies somewhere. The globe is curved. Mercator inflates high latitudes — Greenland is not Africa-sized. Choose a projection for the job (navigation vs equal area).

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Contours are height twins
domains.summary: Contours are height twins. Lines of equal elevation. Tight lines = steep. A ring with hachures can be a depression. Spot heights are the labelled peaks.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: GIS is layers of where
domains.summary: GIS is layers of where. Each layer is a theme (roads, flood, schools). Overlay is the insight. A pin is not a GIS by itself.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A bearing is clockwise from north
domains.summary: A bearing is clockwise from north. 000/360 is north, 090 east. Three digits. Magnetic north is not quite grid north — declination is the gap.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A topographic map is a land contract
domains.summary: A topographic map is a land contract. Grid references (eastings then northings), legend, north arrow. 6-figure refs pinch a 100 m square, not a doormat.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A choropleth is a coloured area story
domains.summary: A choropleth is a coloured area story. Shades for a rate (unemployment %). Colouring raw counts on huge shires lies — Western Australia is not ‘more’ just because it is wide.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Your mental map has holes
domains.summary: Your mental map has holes. People inflate their suburb and shrink the rest. Media inflates some countries. Sketch-from-memory is a bias test.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A satellite image is a sensor, not a visit
domains.summary: A satellite image is a sensor, not a visit. False colour, clouds, resolution, and the date. You cannot see ‘poverty’ from space without a model. Ground-truth exists for a reason.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Australia rides a plate, slowly
domains.summary: Australia rides a plate, slowly. The continent sits on the Indo-Australian Plate, pushing north. Earthquakes exist (Newcastle 1989) even mid-plate. ‘We don’t get quakes’ is folk.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Weather is a day; climate is a script
domains.summary: Weather is a day; climate is a script. Climate is the long pattern (30-year habits). A cold week does not cancel a warming trend. Averages hide extremes that still matter.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: El Niño is a Pacific conversation
domains.summary: El Niño is a Pacific conversation. El Niño often means drier/hotter risks for much of eastern Australia; La Niña wetter. It is not the only dial (IOD, SAM, climate change).

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A mountain wrings the windward side
domains.summary: A mountain wrings the windward side. Moist air rises, cools, rains. The lee is drier — a rain shadow. The Dividing Range helps explain inland dryness, not the whole desert by.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Hadley cells help make deserts
domains.summary: Hadley cells help make deserts. Hot air rises near the equator, rains, then sinks around 30° — dry sinking air. Many deserts sit in that belt, plus cold currents and rain shadows.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Salt can rise when trees fall
domains.summary: Salt can rise when trees fall. Clearing deep-rooted plants lifts watertables and brings salt in some Australian landscapes. Irrigation can do it too. It is a catchment problem,.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A catchment is a bathtub with a tap and a drain
domains.summary: A catchment is a bathtub with a tap and a drain. Ridges define whose rain becomes whose river. Upstream use is a downstream fate. Murray–Darling is a political catchment.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Beaches are moving piles, not furniture
domains.summary: Beaches are moving piles, not furniture. Waves, longshore drift, storms, and headlands. A seawall can starve the next beach of sand. ‘Save our sand’ can steal a neighbour’s.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A biome is a climate-plus-life package
domains.summary: A biome is a climate-plus-life package. Savanna, desert, temperate forest, alpine. Australia’s soils and fire tweak the global poster. A rainforest in Queensland is not ‘the.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A sink stores carbon for a while
domains.summary: A sink stores carbon for a while. Forests, soils, oceans. A bushfire is a rapid source. Planting a tree is not a permanent vault if it burns or dies.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Cities are heat islands
domains.summary: Cities are heat islands. Dark surfaces, less evapotranspiration, waste heat. Nights stay warm. Trees and pale roofs are not decoration.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Liveability is a score with a sponsor
domains.summary: Liveability is a score with a sponsor. Safety, jobs, transit, green, housing cost. A ‘world’s most liveable’ list can skip First Nations, rent, and climate. Whose life?

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Migration has a push and a pull
domains.summary: Migration has a push and a pull. War, drought, work, family, visas. Refugees and skilled migrants are not one pile. A ‘queue’ is a political cartoon of a legal maze.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A pyramid is an age-sex story
domains.summary: A pyramid is an age-sex story. Wide base = lots of kids. A bulge is a baby boom ageing. Japan’s urn shape is not Australia’s, but Australia is ageing too.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Urbanisation is a percent, not a skyline
domains.summary: Urbanisation is a percent, not a skyline. The share of people in cities. A megacity is a size class with informal housing and metro rail in the same frame.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Informal housing is a system, not a mess with no rules
domains.summary: Informal housing is a system, not a mess with no rules. Tenure, work nearby, community organisation. Clearance without a plan is a violence. Services (water, waste) are the.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A global city is a command node
domains.summary: A global city is a command node. Finance, flights, headquarters, culture export. Sydney punches above for a small nation. The back office can be elsewhere.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Mode share is a political geography
domains.summary: Mode share is a political geography. Cars, trains, bikes, feet. Sprawl makes cars ‘necessary’. A freeway is a land-use decision for decades.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Food miles are one slice of impact
domains.summary: Food miles are one slice of impact. Transport energy vs farming energy vs waste. A local hothouse tomato can out-carbon a field tomato from further away. Season matters.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Tourism money can leak
domains.summary: Tourism money can leak. All-inclusive resorts, foreign owners, imported food. A packed lookout can still leave the town poor. Over-tourism is a carrying-capacity issue.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Country is a map that was already here
domains.summary: Country is a map that was already here. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Countries are nations with borders of a kind, not a vague spiritual wallpaper. Dual naming is a.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: The Murray–Darling is a political river
domains.summary: The Murray–Darling is a political river. Irrigation, upstream vs downstream, drought rules, and ecological needs (Menindee, Coorong). Water licences are geography in a spreadsheet.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: The Divide is a weather machine
domains.summary: The Divide is a weather machine. It is not the Andes. It still wrings the east and helps the inland dry. Rivers run east to short, steep coasts or inland to slow plains.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: The Top End has seasons with names
domains.summary: The Top End has seasons with names. Build-up, wet, dry — not four European seasons glued on. Humidity and cyclones are the hazard script.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Arid does not mean empty of life or people
domains.summary: Arid does not mean empty of life or people. Boom-bust rain, huge stations, desert knowledge, mining nodes, and Towns that wait on a wet year. ‘Dead centre’ is a tourist line.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Australians hug the coast
domains.summary: Australians hug the coast. Climate, colonial ports, and the Divide’s wet side. The empty map is a population map, not a ‘unused’ map.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A mining town is a clock
domains.summary: A mining town is a clock. Boom, FIFO, bust, rehab. The ore is a place; the price is global. When the clock stops, geography remains (holes, housing, who left).

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: The urban–bush interface is a designed risk
domains.summary: The urban–bush interface is a designed risk. Houses in trees, fuel, slope, day of 40° and a northerly. Building codes and leave-or-stay are geography plus policy.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: The Reef is a living structure with a temperature limit
domains.summary: The Reef is a living structure with a temperature limit. Coral bleaching is a heat-and-stress story. Tourism, farming runoff, and cyclones stack. It is not ‘pretty rocks’.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Antarctica is a treaty with a climate file
domains.summary: Antarctica is a treaty with a climate file. Australia claims a slice; the Treaty freezes sovereignty fights for science. Ice cores and krill are global. Tourism is a pressure.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Hazard × vulnerability = the disaster
domains.summary: Hazard × vulnerability = the disaster. A cyclone over an empty reef vs over a tin-roof town. Risk is not the wind alone. Poverty and building codes sit in the equation.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Who cooked, who burns
domains.summary: Who cooked, who burns. High emitters vs high-vulnerability places (low atolls, heat in western Sydney). Justice is a geography of responsibility and capacity.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Waste is a flow with a sink that leaks
domains.summary: Waste is a flow with a sink that leaks. Export bans, local recycling limits, and rivers to the sea. ‘Recycled’ on a packet can be a wish. Reduce is upstream.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Scarcity can be physical or political
domains.summary: Scarcity can be physical or political. There is enough water in some basins until licences and seasons say no. Desal is energy-expensive insurance. A drought is not only ‘no.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A forest is a carbon, water, and people system
domains.summary: A forest is a carbon, water, and people system. Clearing for cattle/palm/soy has teleconnections — your supermarket. Illegal vs legal is a governance layer. Primary forest is not.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A T-shirt is a global production line
domains.summary: A T-shirt is a global production line. Cotton water, dye rivers, sewn in one country, worn twice, dumped. Geography of labour plus geography of waste.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: Energy mix is a map of wires and vetoes
domains.summary: Energy mix is a map of wires and vetoes. Sun and wind are located. Transmission, storage, and coal towns’ next job are the geographic problem. NIMBY vs supply is a real tension.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A border is a decision with a fence optional
domains.summary: A border is a decision with a fence optional. Rivers move, mountains sit, rulers drew lines. A hard border for COVID was a health geography. A maritime EEZ is a resource border.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: A chokepoint is a narrow power
domains.summary: A chokepoint is a narrow power. Malacca, Hormuz, Suez. A stuck ship is a syllabus. Australia’s trade rides some of these whether we like it or not.

domains.subject: geography
domains.title: GDP is a blunt liveability stick
